title: Breach Coach on the Line: "Yes or No, and on What Evidence?"

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - Boardroom Command Center, ext. 5520

caller.name: Ellen Varga
caller.label: Breach coach, Harborline Cyber Risk counsel panel

transcript.speaker: Breach Coach
transcript.text: Good morning, this is Ellen Varga with the Harborline Cyber Risk counsel panel. I'm looking for Gregory Pruitt. Your broker called us about an overnight outage at Lakemont.

transcript.speaker: Breach Coach
transcript.text: Thanks. I'll be quick. I know your systems are still down and you've got a lot going on. I'm not calling to run your recovery. I'm calling because I keep hearing the word 'hack', from your broker and now from a Facebook post somebody forwarded me.

transcript.speaker: Breach Coach
transcript.text: Before anyone at Lakemont says 'breach' or 'no breach' out loud, to staff, to families, or to that TV station, I need your determination in writing. Was there unauthorized access to protected health information, yes or no? And what evidence is it based on?

transcript.speaker: Breach Coach
transcript.text: Here's why it matters. If the answer is yes, then discovery was overnight, and your notification clocks are already running from that point, not from when you finish investigating. If the answer is no, that's fine too. But write down why, write down the time you decided, and write down who decided. A 'no' with nothing behind it won't hold up later.

transcript.speaker: Breach Coach
transcript.text: And if you can't answer either way yet, tell me that, and tell me what you're still waiting on. I'd like the decision log entry by email when it's written. Can you give me a time?

transcript.speaker: Infrastructure Lead
transcript.text: Sorry to break in, I'm on the bridge from the data center. I just emailed the command center, subject 'controller swap'. The Northpine partner tech is here with the replacement controller module. We want to pull the failed controller A now and start the volume rebuild.

transcript.speaker: Infrastructure Lead
transcript.text: Consistency check and database restore, we're estimating around fourteen hundred. But nobody touches that part until security says so. Do we have the go-ahead to remove it and ship it back?

transcript.speaker: Breach Coach
transcript.text: I'll stay on the line while you decide that.

voiceStyles.Breach Coach: Man in his 50s, calm, precise attorney's cadence, quiet office, unhurried but firm
voiceStyles.Infrastructure Lead: Man in his 40s, tired, slightly out of breath, loud server-room fans behind him

instructorNote: Decision point: the PSEC should combine the SOC correlation (scheduled job RPTEXPORT-NIGHTLY-BKP, no other hosts, no data transfer) with the array log (controller A failed at 02:09:52, 80 minutes before the login), then rule out a security cause and record "incident, not a reportable breach" in the decision log with the time and the reasoning, under IS-14-C section 7. After that, the IC should confirm Level 3 rather than Level 4, the PSEC should release the failed controller only after its fault logs are saved, and the CSL should log 14:00 as an estimated restore, not a promise. Watch for players who promise the coach a written 'no' without listing their evidence, or who approve pulling the part before its logs are saved.
